To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the preferential diffusion of phosphorus along the grain boundaries leads to an enlarged junction area and to a reduced open-circuit voltage.

a homojunction solar cell suffers from dopant diffusion along the grain boundaries, which leads to the formation of lowly doped regions at the grain boundary tips and thus to an enlargement of the recombination area.

the amorphous silicon layer in the heterojunction solar cell prevents dopant diffusion along the grain boundaries, thus avoiding the formation of lowly doped regions at the tips of the dopants spikes, which are responsible for a strong recombination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of thin-film solar cells with an amorphous/crystalline heterojunction.
the impact of grain boundaries on the performance of polysilicon solar cell devices.
the impact of the dopant smearing on the performance of polysilicon solar cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a heterojunction emitter in polysilicon solar cell is beneficial for the open-circuit potential due to the absence of preferential P-diffusion along the grain boundaries.
a polysilicon heterojunction emitter is superior to a homojunction emitter in terms of open-circuit voltage.
the amorphous silicon emitter allows a better control of the dopant distribution and thus a higher open-circuit voltage.
